transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aria Patel (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (BluePeak Head of ML), Priya Desai (BluePeak VP Eng), Evan Li (BluePeak SRE)

Summary: quick recap provided at start; main ask: clearer cost path to Dedicated, SOC2 docs, run a performance benchmark to reproduce latency spike from last month

00:00 Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining for the QBR and health check, uh we scheduled 50 minutes, we'll do a quick usage/cost review then Liam will run through his notes on the latency incident and recommendations then Aria will cover roadmap and next steps
00:18 Mark Reynolds: sounds good, thanks Sofia; busy week so appreciate the summary notes you sent earlier
00:30 Priya Desai: quick note we brought Evan from SRE because they saw the 95th percentile jump last month and want to make sure it's covered for procurement
00:44 Sofia Martinez: yep, perfect; quick housekeeping, we'll record this and share the deck, and Liam will share the SOC2/ISO bundle after the call
01:05 Liam Chen: ok jumping in on usage — BluePeak has been ramping on the customer-support generative feature, tokens up ~3.2x month over month, right? Mark is that what's driving it
01:22 Mark Reynolds: yeah that's right, the auto-responder and summary flows especially; we also increased context window to 8k for many jobs which increased token usage
01:38 Sofia Martinez: just to add from our side, we see the call mix shifting toward long-form summaries which increases per-request tokens; that explains the cost increase
01:52 Priya Desai: cost is now a top concern for our finance team, they asked for a few levers — batching, quantization, and maybe Dedicated pricing. can you walk through the math quickly
02:10 Sofia Martinez: sure — on hosted, your unit cost went up with the increased tokens and some of the bigger models; our recommendation is a 3-step plan: 1) immediate batching and cache tuning to lower per-token bill, 2) targeted quantization for the high-throughput endpoints, 3) evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit ops
02:36 Liam Chen: to add: with our optimized batching we usually see 20-35% token cost reduction for long-form features. quantization (8-bit) often gives additional 15-25% depending on tolerance for small quality delta
02:55 Evan Li: do you have examples from other finance customers on quality delta after quantization? we can't tolerate hallucinations on regulatory answers
03:12 Liam Chen: yeah logically — we can run an eval set you provide; in a few finance pilots we've seen negligible end-user impact on our 8-bit profiles but we always recommend evals across your prompt set
03:30 Mark Reynolds: ok that makes sense, we'll share a representative prompt suite
03:40 Sofia Martinez: moving to the reliability incident — Liam, you took the lead on triage
03:46 Liam Chen: yeah, so on Oct 21 we saw a latency spike affecting the 95th percentile across a subset of hosts; initial triage: increased cold-starts due to model rolling and a temporary hotspot on KV cache eviction. there was also a mis-routed fallback that increased upstream calls
04:10 Evan Li: we saw errors in our logs with timeouts to the inference service at around 18:14 UTC, that maps to your spike
04:22 Liam Chen: right — root cause was an interplay between aggressive autoscale burst plus a mis-configured cache TTL which caused cache thrash; we pushed a patch to smooth TTLs and adjusted the autoscale policy to prefer warm spare instances
04:43 Priya Desai: ok so is this a recurring risk on hosted? we were trying to decide between hosted vs Dedicated primarily for reliability control
04:55 Liam Chen: hosted has a high-availability SLA, but Dedicated gives you isolation: no noisy neighbor and you control scaling policies. for customers with strict SLOs, Dedicated is preferred. that said we can also implement stronger guardrails on hosted to reduce recurrence
05:15 Sofia Martinez: financially, Dedicated becomes attractive when steady-state throughput crosses a certain threshold — from your usage profile it looks like a Dedicated pilot could pay off if you commit to capacity for peak windows
05:32 Mark Reynolds: what commitment levels are we talking about? quarter? year? how granular is burst capacity
05:42 Sofia Martinez: typically monthly or annual committed units; we do offer burst credits for short peaks. I'll send you a model in the next step that shows break-even points for 3-6-12 month commitments
05:58 Evan Li: another question: network setup for Dedicated in our VPC — how do you handle egress and private peering, and do you support HSM KMS for key material
06:15 Liam Chen: yes, Dedicated can run in a customer VPC with private peering and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key encryption. note: we call this Redwood Private for the fully customer-managed control plane; the Dedicated offering is reserved capacity with VPC options
06:38 Priya Desai: great, can you share the network diagram and an example runbook for failover
06:45 Liam Chen: will do — I'll add the diagram to the SOC2 bundle share
06:55 Aria Patel: quick check on roadmap — Mark, what features are you most interested in from Redwood's roadmap this quarter?
07:04 Mark Reynolds: improved KV cache persistence across restarts and better tracing for token-level cost attribution, also more model quantization profiles exposed in the console
07:18 Aria Patel: on tracing and cost attribution we've got a rollout next month for token-level labeling in the console and a new export to BigQuery; the KV persistence work is in our Q1 roadmap but I can push to prioritize if it helps your procurement timeline
07:36 Priya Desai: that would be helpful, procurement wants to see timeline commitments
07:42 Aria Patel: understood, I'll include a roadmap snapshot and potential prioritization with target dates
07:50 Sofia Martinez: let's talk benchmarks — Evan you mentioned wanting a run to reproduce the Oct spike; what's the workload profile you want to test
08:01 Evan Li: a steady stream of 200 concurrent sessions, average request size 3.5k tokens, spikes to 600 concurrent for onboarding flows. we want p95 < 800ms for short prompts and p95 < 2s for long-form summaries
08:20 Liam Chen: ok that's doable, we'll mirror your network conditions as best as possible; we'll propose a 3-phase benchmark: lab run on hosted, lab run on Dedicated pilot, and then a short in-prod canary with reduced traffic
08:36 Mark Reynolds: timeline for that? procurement needs results before the 25th
08:41 Liam Chen: propose lab runs this week and a canary by the 20th — depends on SOC2 doc delivery and access to a representative prompt set
08:52 Priya Desai: fine, we'll aim to provide prompt set and test accounts by Friday 11/13
09:00 Sofia Martinez: next on costs, quick breakdown — we noticed a single high-volume endpoint accounts for ~55% of tokens; you should consider offloading some pre/post-processing to client side or batch requests server-side to reduce tokens
09:20 Mark Reynolds: we can try batching but there's a latency sensitivity for some flows; can batching be tuned per endpoint
09:30 Liam Chen: yes — you can have per-route batching configs; we also support adaptive batching that balances latency and throughput. we'll include recommended configs in the follow-up doc
09:44 Priya Desai: anything about model selection? we saw you had a note about switching to a smaller model for short replies
09:52 Sofia Martinez: correct — one of the immediate wins is to route short reply traffic to a small, cheaper model and reserve the larger models for long-context summaries. Smart routing and fallback policies handle that automatically if you set the route rules
10:12 Evan Li: curious about audit logs and retention, our compliance team wants 7 years of immutable logs for specific flows
10:24 Liam Chen: our Private on-prem option supports long-term archiving and integrations with customer SIEMs; for hosted, we offer retention tiers and can ship logs to your storage with encryption at rest. we'll include the retention options and costs in the doc
10:41 Mark Reynolds: procurement will also ask about liability and indemnity; is there a standard contract for Dedicated customers
10:50 Sofia Martinez: yes we have an enterprise contract template; our legal team can work with yours — I'll loop in our legal AE and follow up
11:00 Priya Desai: ok good. any known limitations for the Dedicated pilot in terms of model variants or quantization support
11:08 Liam Chen: Dedicated supports most open-model variants we onboard, and quantization profiles are supported but there are edge cases for some bleeding-edge topologies — we'll list supported models for your pilot
11:24 Mark Reynolds: on the operational side, how do SLO alerts integrate with our PagerDuty
11:31 Evan Li: yes and how do we get token-level billing into our internal chargeback system
11:38 Aria Patel: we have webhook integrations for SLO alerts and an export for per-route cost that can be pushed to BigQuery or S3; we'll send a setup guide with sample Terraform for the integrations
11:54 Sofia Martinez: ok let's recap action items and owners quickly
12:02 Sofia Martinez: Sofia to send dedicated pricing model and break-even analysis by 11/12
12:09 Liam Chen: Liam to share SOC2/ISO docs, network diagram, and a list of supported model/quant profiles by 11/10
12:18 Evan Li: BluePeak to provide prompt suite, test accounts, and a list of top endpoints by 11/13
12:26 Aria Patel: Aria to send a roadmap snapshot and possible prioritization timelines by 11/12
12:40 Mark Reynolds: thanks everyone — we'll review the materials and aim to sign off on pilot scope next week
12:50 Sofia Martinez: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and the pricing deep dive
12:56 Priya Desai: thanks all, appreciate the thoroughness
13:00 Meeting end

Notes: transcript includes typical transcription artifacts — names occasionally mis-heard in the automated text; some technical terms appear with variations (e.g., K-V cache, Redwood Dedi, quant profiles). Links shared during call: /link/bluepeak-qbr-deck, /link/soc2-bundle, /link/benchmark-plan
